subject: biology
title: Plant systems: water and nutrient transport

scenes.heading: Plant systems: water and nutrient transport
scenes.sub: How a gum tree lifts water with no heart or pump
scenes.say: A tall gum tree lifts water from its roots to leaves dozens of metres up, with no heart or pump. How? Meet the plant's two transport systems: xylem and phloem.

scenes.heading: Xylem vs phloem

right.title: Phloem
points: Up or down: source to sink

scenes.say: Xylem carries water and minerals, upward only. It's made of dead, hollow tubes stiffened with lignin, and uses no ATP. Phloem flows food. It carries sugars, mainly sucrose, up or down, in living sieve tubes with companion cells.

scenes.heading: Roots and transpiration
scenes.say: Root hairs increase the surface area of roots. Minerals enter by active transport, and water follows by osmosis. At the other end, water evaporates inside the leaf and escapes as vapour through stomata. That's transpiration.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A conga line: the leader steps forward and the whole line follows
scenes.science: Transpiration pulls; cohesion holds the water column together
scenes.breaks: Dancers use their own energy. Water doesn't: the sun drives evaporation, and xylem uses no ATP.
scenes.say: Picture a conga line going up the stairs. When the leader steps forward, the whole line follows. Transpiration is the leader pulling at the top. Cohesion, water sticking to water, holds the line together. Adhesion is like gripping the rail. But the energy comes from the sun, not ATP.

scenes.heading: Faster transpiration when…
scenes.say: Clothes dry fastest on a hot, dry, windy, sunny day. Plants transpire fastest in the same conditions: high temperature, low humidity, wind and more light.

scenes.heading: Translocation in the phloem
steps: Sucrose actively loaded at the source
Water enters by osmosis: pressure rises
scenes.say: Phloem moves sugar from a source, like a leaf, to a sink, like roots or fruit. Sucrose is loaded at the source, using ATP from companion cells. Water follows by osmosis and pressure builds. At the sink, sucrose is removed, so pressure falls. The pressure difference pushes the sap along.

scenes.heading: Ringing a tree
scenes.question: A ring of bark (containing phloem, not xylem) is removed from a trunk. Bark above the ring swells, and the roots die. Why?
lines: Phloem is removed with the bark
Sugars can't move down past the ring
They build up above it: swelling
Answer: roots get no sugar, can't respire
scenes.say: Remove a ring of bark, and you remove the phloem. Sugars can't travel down past the ring, so they build up and the bark above swells. The roots get no sugar, so they can't respire, and they die. The xylem is undamaged, so the leaves don't wilt straight away.

points: Guard cells open and close stomata
scenes.say: Quick recap. Xylem carries water and minerals upward. Phloem carries sugars from source to sink. Transpiration pull and cohesion lift water without ATP. And guard cells open and close stomata, balancing carbon dioxide in against water out. Now try the practice questions!
